minutes.headline: Committee heard the HR consultant's draft salary grid, deferred review, and set a placeholder town meeting article.
minutes.summary: The HR consultant, calling in from vacation, gave an overview of the draft compensation study and a shorter salary grid. Members said they received the materials too late to comment, so the grid and the job descriptions were pushed to a meeting the next Monday. The committee discussed a blank placeholder article to meet the March 20 submission deadline and a motion was made on it. The captions show no vote result.

budget_items.what_was_said: The consultant said many towns adopt the grid in year one and let people see step increases the next year, to avoid a large immediate cost.
The consultant said steps are kept at or below a level that stays sustainable under Proposition 2 1/2, since steps are owed even in a year without cost of living increases.

budget_items.what_was_said: The consultant compared the old grid's gaps between grades with best-practice ranges for entry, mid and executive levels.

budget_items.topic: Cost of placing employees on new grid
budget_items.what_was_said: Members want a cost analysis comparing immediate adoption with delayed adoption, noting some top steps are below current salaries.

what_happened.line: The committee heard the HR consultant's draft compensation study and shorter salary grid, but members said the materials came too late to review.
The salary grid and job descriptions were pushed to the next meeting rather than discussed substantively.
A motion was made on the HR Director's proposed town meeting article; the captions do not capture the vote result.
The committee agreed a blank placeholder article is enough to meet the March 20 article deadline, with the grid to be finalized by about March 30.
A public commenter objected that the consultant's report was not shared with employees in advance so they could give input.

why_it_matters: The salary grid sets what town employees are paid and what each step costs, so it feeds the town budget, which is mostly taxes, and the compensation article residents may be asked to vote on at town meeting.
The committee has not yet seen a cost comparison of adopting the grid at once versus phasing it in, so the size of the budget effect is not yet on the record.
The vote on the article is not audible in the captions, so the outcome should be confirmed from the official minutes.
